patch.value: Consume the canonical attestation gate instead of carrying a copy of it

This repository carried its own vendored copy of the publish-attestation scanner and verifier. That gate decides whether an artefact may reach the registry, so a false pass is the failure that matters, and a copy frozen at any point in the canonical implementation fix sequence still admits every construction closed after that point.

Measured with the fleet bypass corpus (scripts/attest-corpus/check.sh in the companion), run through this repository own verify() against a throwaway git repository, which is the level CI runs. AFTER is 7 of 38 - the same seven every converged repository reports, because they all run the same published code. Every one of the seven is open in the canonical implementation rather than here, and all are closed by unbraind/pm-ops#100, so they close here with an ordinary version bump.

That identity is the point, not the count. Before convergence this repository had a posture no pm-ops release could reach; after it, one release moves it along with every sibling.

The scanner is deleted, the verifier becomes a thin launcher over the published pm-ops/attestation export, and the suite no longer re-tests the shell model - that belongs with the implementation. It asserts instead that this repository is still a CONSUMER: no local scanner, the launcher re-exporting the package own functions BY REFERENCE so a wrapper cannot start a re-fork unnoticed, and the resolved gate still refusing an unattested publish.

No local shell-command-scan.ts remains and the launcher imports pm-ops/attestation; The launcher re-exports the package's own functions by reference, asserted in the suite; The corpus reads the same seven cases as every other converged repository

value.author: claude
value.text:
Review round: three findings, all real, all in the same class - the guard asserted less than its comment claimed.

Every reviewer on this wave (Greptile P2 on seven repositories, CodeRabbit Major on two, Sourcery on one) independently raised the same gap: re-export identity pins the IMPORTED binding, not the one runIfMain actually calls. A future edit could divert only the executed path and leave every other assertion green. The entry-point test now captures what runIfMain writes and asserts it equals the package's own report(verify(fixture)) byte for byte - a local reimplementation would have to reproduce the canonical auditor's exact failure wording to pass, and reproducing it is being it. Proven not vacuous: diverting only the executed path to a local verify makes the test fail while re-export identity and the exit code still pass.

Greptile also called the shebang matrix too narrow. Widened to six states: #!/bin/bash, #!/bin/sh and #!/usr/bin/env sh must make the file shell input; #!/usr/bin/env node, #!/usr/bin/env python3 and no shebang must not.

CodeRabbit found the shebang test could pass for the wrong reason: it depends on this file's prose naming the command it guards, and if the prose stopped mentioning it every case would read 'not shell input' and the test would go green having proved nothing. The precondition is now asserted.

Also on CodeRabbit's point, the fixture no longer commits: the gate discovers files through git ls-files, which reads the index, so staging is sufficient and committing made the fixture depend on ambient git identity configuration for no gain.

message: review round: entry-path identity, shebang breadth, fixture precondition

author: claude

value.author: claude
value.text:
Round 2 finding, and it landed AFTER the round-1 fix rather than before it - Greptile read the new code and answered the challenge the PR comment had posed.

The single-fixture byte comparison did not prove what its comment claimed. A local verifier that hardcodes that one report satisfies it, the workflow-name assertion, and the re-export identity check simultaneously, while diverging on every other publish shape.

The comparison now runs over four structurally different shapes, each exercising a different decision in the auditor: a plain unattested publish (is a publish recognised), an unresolved program via command substitution (is an unprovable program audited anyway), a foreign publisher (does pnpm count), and an attested publish (is a correct one left alone, exit code untouched). A local implementation matching all four across every decision would be a reimplementation of the auditor, which is what was being ruled out.

Proven against both attacks: diverting the executed path to a local verify fails, and hardcoding the FIRST fixture's exact report - the attack named in the finding - also fails, because the other three shapes disagree.

The residual limit is stated in the test rather than left implied: ESM offers no way to observe a call target from outside the module, so this is agreement across a shape space, not call-site identity. That is precisely why the space is varied instead of a single case.

message: round 2: one fixture was satisfiable by a hardcoded report

value.text:
Three more findings, all correct.

Greptile: the single-fixture byte comparison was satisfiable by a local verifier that hardcodes that one report - the attack was built and passed 6/6 against the old test. The comparison now runs four structurally different shapes (plain unattested, unresolved program via command substitution, foreign publisher, attested), and the same hardcode fails because the other three disagree. The residual limit is written into the test: ESM offers no way to observe a call target from outside the module, so this is agreement across a shape space, not call-site identity.

CodeRabbit: the launcher docstring still claimed the suite reproduces 'all three states' after the matrix grew to six. That is the same copied-text-carries-the-error pattern this convergence exists to end, this time in text written today. Corrected in all thirteen repositories with an open convergence PR; seven already-merged ones carry the same stale sentence and need a follow-up.

CodeRabbit: two sites built the same throwaway git repository. Extracted to withTrackedFixture, which documents why staging without committing suffices - the gate reads git ls-files, so a commit adds only a dependency on ambient git identity configuration. The hardcode attack was re-run after the extraction to confirm it did not weaken.

message: round 2: shape matrix, docstring state count, shared fixture helper
